label: conj:braid-boost-inertial-equivalence
title: Braid-boost inertial equivalence
html:
Let (\mathbf{C}, A, au) be an archimedean quantum observable universe over \mathbb{R} with substrate parameter q > 1 and causal-cone speed c_q = 1/(q-1) (speed of light). For every braid class eta, the kinematic inertia m_{\mathrm{in}}( eta) that eta carries as a worldline under a boost along the causal cone equals its Frobenius--Hopf holonomy mass (mass identity):

  m_{\mathrm{in}}( eta) = \mathfrak{m}( eta).

The statement has content only once m_{\mathrm{in}}( eta) is defined without reference to \mathfrak{m}( eta), through an action of boosts on braid classes. No such action is defined in this work. Two routes are recorded.

  1. Reeb-clock kinetic coefficient. Write \hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} and \iota_\xi abla for the Reeb contraction of the connection in the categorical Dirac operator. Scaling the Reeb contraction by a clock rate \omega turns the traced categorical Hamiltonian Lagrangian into a_2\,\omega^2 + a_1\,\omega + a_0, and m_{\mathrm{in}} = 2a_2 = 2\hbar_q^2\, au(\iota_\xi abla \circ \iota_\xi abla) is the natural kinetic coefficient. Under non-abelian Stokes descent the trace au(\iota_\xi abla \circ \iota_\xi abla) is the Casimir-weighted, regular trace of the Hecke algebra, not the Markov trace. This candidate fails. In H_2(q) and H_3(q) the ratio m_{\mathrm{in}}/\mathfrak{m} is a non-constant rational function that depends on eta, and at q = 1 one has m_{\mathrm{in}} = 0 while \mathfrak{m} = 2^{c( eta)}, with c( eta) the number of components of the closure. Any candidate of the form \hbar_q^2 times a trace that is finite at q = 1 fails for the same reason.
  2. Boost action on the affine causality cone. On the contact affine chart with homogeneous coordinates [\omega : u] (Reeb and horizontal components), the affine coordinate is Z = u/\omega and the causality cone is |Z| < c_q with null points Z = \pm c_q. A binary quadratic form vanishing at both null points is a multiple of c_q^2\omega^2 - u^2, so the cone alone fixes a Lorentzian form. The projective maps fixing both null points act on Z as boosts Z \mapsto (Z + v)/(1 + vZ/c_q^2). They compose by relativistic velocity addition and preserve the cone |Z| < c_q. Eliminating an einbein from the cone form gives the worldline Lagrangian -m\,c_q\sqrt{c_q^2 - v^2} used in the mass--energy equivalence. So the boost group and the worldline are derived from the cone rather than postulated. The parameter m stays free: the conjecture now says that a braid class's traced Lagrangian along a worldline is boost-covariant in this sense, with coefficient m = \mathfrak{m}( eta). That remains open.

What a proof needs. Write the traced square of the Dirac operator D = \Omega_H\, abla + \Omega_R\,\iota_\xi abla as A\,\Omega_R^2 + B\,\Omega_R\Omega_H + C\,\Omega_H^2, with A = au igl((\iota_\xi abla)^2 igr), B = au( abla\,\iota_\xi abla + \iota_\xi abla\, abla) and C = au( abla^2). This form is boost-covariant, that is, proportional to c_q^2\Omega_R^2 - \Omega_H^2, exactly when B = 0 and A = -c_q^2\,C. If A, B and C do not depend on q, covariance can hold at only one value of q unless A = C = 0, since distinct q > 1 give distinct c_q. The concrete Dirac operator of the substrate (connection \mathrm{ad}_\Omega with a q-independent Reeb map) has non-zero A, B and C, with C twice the discriminant of \Omega. For it, covariance would single out one value of q from the substrate data. A proof of the conjecture therefore needs two steps, neither of which is constructed in this work:

  1. a Dirac datum attached to each braid class eta whose traces scale as A/C = -1/(q-1)^2 for every q > 1, with B = 0;
  2. the identification of the resulting boost-covariant coefficient with \mathfrak{m}( eta).

A natural candidate for the first step takes abla and \iota_\xi abla from the q-dependent Hecke representation of eta, where the traces vary with q. Whether some such choice satisfies the scaling for every q, without selecting the operators to fit it, is open.

If the conjecture holds, the rest energy of a braid class is \mathfrak{E}( eta) = \mathfrak{m}( eta)\,c_q^2 (mass--energy equivalence).
heading: Conjecture
